seo_title: Cost of Living in Varna 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Varna per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Bulgaria's maritime capital: beaches, a mild climate, affordable rent and a large Russian-speaking community. A genuine path to residency through buying property and a peaceful life by the sea with EU prospects.
pros: A seaside city with beaches running along the entire boulevard
Prices lower than Sofia at the same level of comfort
A large Russian-speaking community dating back to the USSR
Easy property purchases and a clear path to residency
Direct flights from Russia in the holiday season
cons: Strong seasonality: tourists in summer, the city empties in winter
Some services only operate from May to October
An old housing stock; new developments cost more
Overcast and damp by the sea in winter

visa_steps.title: Schengen visa
visa_steps.description: Bulgaria has been in Schengen since 2024 — you need a C or D visa via the embassy.

visa_steps.title: Residency through business or property
visa_steps.description: Buying a home or setting up a Bulgarian LLC grants the right to a 1-year residence permit with renewal.

visa_steps.title: EIK and tax registration
visa_steps.description: A standard procedure through a notary and the Registry Agency.

visa_steps.title: Account and insurance
visa_steps.description: UBB and DSK work with Russians who hold a residence permit. Health insurance is mandatory.

visa_steps.title: Municipal registration
visa_steps.description: Registration at your place of residence after obtaining a residence permit — needed for healthcare and school.

faq.question: How is Varna different from Sofia?
faq.answer: The sea, a more resort-like pace, slightly cheaper and warmer. But there's less work and worse healthcare.

faq.question: How is swimming in Varna?
faq.answer: The season runs June to September, with water up to +25°C. The beach is sandy and has free sections.

faq.question: Which district should I choose in Varna?
faq.answer: The centre and the Greek Quarter — for living. Levski, Chayka — modern developments. Vinitsa — quieter and cheaper.

faq.question: How are the internet and infrastructure in Varna?
faq.answer: Fibre at 100+ Mbps for 1,500 rubles. 4G/5G across the city.

faq.question: Is Varna safe?
faq.answer: Yes, one of the safest cities in Bulgaria. Crime is low.

faq.question: Is it worth buying property in Varna?
faq.answer: Prices are affordable (from €50,000 for a studio by the sea), but the rental market is seasonal — it's easy to let in summer.

reviews.text: I moved my family and business to Varna: a home by the sea, my child in an international school. Winter is dreary, but summer makes up for it.
We rent an apartment in a new building for €500 and work remotely. The sea, peace and quiet, and an understandable Europe without the culture shock.
